context.body: Joab was told, “Behold, the king weeps and mourns for Absalom.”.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The army enters quietly as David mourns; Joab accuses him of shaming loyal servants, David returns to the gate, and messengers call Judah to restore the king.
observations.label: Joab confronts grief and Judah is summoned: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps David, Joab, soldiers, Israel, Judah, Zadok, Abiathar, Amasa, and royal relatives, Mahanaim’s gate and the road toward the Jordan, mourning, rebuking, rising, sitting at the gate, debating, sending, promising command, and returning hearts visible within David's story or later memory.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 19:1–15 as its own exile, return, and rebellion David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places grief is redirected into public presence and political return inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
